rawFindings.title: Incorrect usage of trust proxy function leads to inconsistent behavior
rawFindings.explanation: The trust proxy function is called with only one argument instead of two. The original code used `trust(this.connection.remoteAddress, 0)` to consider the first proxy hop. The new code omits the second argument, potentially causing the function to behave differently and break proxy trust logic affecting req.protocol and req.secure.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original call to include the hop count argument: `trust(this.connection.remoteAddress, 0)`.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect handling of trust function in req.protocol getter
rawFindings.explanation: The original code called the trust function with two arguments: the remote address and 0. The updated code calls the trust function with the remote address only, omitting the hop count argument. This potentially changes the meaning of the trust function call and prevents proper trust calculation when 'trust proxy' is set to a hop count, thus possibly leading to incorrect determination of protocol (http/https).
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original call to the trust function with the hop count, i.e., use: if (!trust(this.connection.remoteAddress, 0))

rawFindings.title: Incorrect `trust` function call in `req.protocol` getter
rawFindings.explanation: In the `req.protocol` getter, the `trust` function is called without the second argument (hop count), whereas it is expected to be called with the remote address and a hop count (usually 0). Omitting the hop count can cause incorrect trust evaluation of the proxy and thus incorrect protocol detection when behind proxies.
rawFindings.suggestion: Change the line `if (!trust(this.connection.remoteAddress)) {` to `if (!trust(this.connection.remoteAddress, 0)) {` to correctly pass the hop count argument expected by the trust function.
